https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: A murder investigation has been launched after two people died in a house fire at a property in Grangetown, Middlesbrough. Photograph: Tom Wilkinson/PA View image in fullscreen A murder investigation has been launched after two people died in a house fire at a property in Grangetown, Middlesbrough. Photograph: Tom Wilkinson/PA UK news Murder investigation launched after two die in Middlesbrough house fire Cleveland police not ruling out links to organised crime, as fire comes amid force’s investigation into fatal A66 crash Mark Brown North of England correspondent Wed 26 Aug 2026 08.09 EDT Last modified on Wed 26 Aug 2026 08.24 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A murder investigation has been launched after a house fire in Middlesbrough killed two people, with police not ruling out links to organised crime. The blaze in the early hours of Wednesday came as police continued to investigate the wider circumstances around a collision on Saturday on the A66 that killed seven people, including two police officers. Cleveland police said officers were called at 5.23am to reports of a house fire in the Grangetown area of Middlesbrough. Two people died in the fire and a woman was in hospital in Newcastle in a critical condition, police said. A further three people sustained non-life-threatening injuries and were receiving treatment in hospital, a spokesperson added. Supt Emily Harrison, Redcar and Cleveland’s local policing commander, said: “We are working to establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened, but we are keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time.” View image in fullscreen Cleveland fire brigade said it sent six fire engines and an incident command unit to the scene of the Grangetown blaze. Photograph: Tom Wilkinson/PA The blaze was about two miles from the scene of Saturday’s collision in which a Volkswagen Passat, travelling in the wrong direction, crashed head-on into a police vehicle on the A66. PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, were killed in the collision. The five occupants of the Volkswagen Passat were also killed, and pronounced dead at the scene. They have been named as Cole Worthy and Theo Rae, both 17, Makai Saddington, 18, and Michael Robert Cahill and Jacob Matusiak, both 23. Since then Cleveland police said they had “continued to disrupt those suspected of being involved in serious and organised crime”. That effort has resulted in 17 arrests. Wayne Fox, the assistant chief constable responsible for the strategic leadership of the investigation, said: “This has been a fast-moving and complex investigation, with significant links to serious and organised criminal activity. The events of that tragic night will have a lasting and profound impact on the Cleveland area and the communities we seek to protect. “We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident, and to bring all those responsible to justice. Our robust response will continue in the weeks and months to come, as we continue to tackle those that seek to cause harm to our communities and tackle serious and organised crime.” Cleveland fire brigade said it had sent six fire engines and an incident command unit to the scene of the Grangetown blaze. A spokesperson said road closures were in place in the surrounding area and asked members of the public to avoid the area where possible. Adam Brook, a Redcar and Cleveland borough councillor for Grangetown, said the fire was “absolutely devastating”, but urged people not to speculate or “share unconfirmed information”. He said: “Many residents have been in touch with me throughout the morning, and I know there is understandably a great deal of concern. However, I would urge people not to speculate or share unconfirmed information.” Explore more on these topics UK news news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

They include Arvind Kejriwal, leader of the Aam Aadmi Party and former chief minister of Delhi . "It's official... we are living under an absolute dictatorship," Kejriwal wrote on X. Mamata Banerjee, who lost power as West Bengal's chief minister earlier this year, was also detained. Pinarayi Vijayan, a communist leader who headed the southern state of Kerala until May, was among those detained. Rahul Gandhi, leader of India's opposition Congress party , called the crackdown an act of "cowardice" and described Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, right-wing, Hindu nationalist RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval as "the villains of this story" who were "slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space." Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul Gandhi's sister and a Congress MP, wrote in a social media post: "India is not a democracy anymore. It is a dictatorship being run by Mr. Narendra Modi and Mr. Amit Shah." Opposition parties and critics have warned that the electoral-roll revision exercise could strip millions of people of their voting rights and give an advantage to Prime Minister Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission of India has rejected allegations of wrongdoing, saying the "special intensive revision" aims to remove duplicate and ineligible voters. The protests echo the CJP's mass mobilization in July, which forced the then education minister to resign over an examination scandal. This time, demonstrators are demanding the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), an independent nonprofit organization that promotes press freedom and defends journalists' rights worldwide, has called on Delhi Police to immediately release all detained journalists and media workers. This comes amid a reported crackdown on protesters attempting to reach the national capital, specifically central Delhi, to protest against India's chief election commissioner over alleged misconduct. The Airbus A320 landed safely with 51 passengers and six crew members aboard after reportedly receiving a bomb threat near the Bulgarian-Romanian border. "During the flight, ​on the border with Romania, the crew reported a ​bomb threat signal and decided to land in Sofia extraordinarily," the Bulgarian Transport ​Ministry said ​in a ⁠statement. Austrian Airlines gave the all-clear on Monday morning, confirming in a statement that "no danger was identified" after a search of the aircraft, passengers and crew. It added that the flight continued to Vienna with all the affected passengers. Fighter jet escorts plane The Airbus A320 plane was flying from Tel Aviv for Vienna but was diverted to Sofia in Bulgaria at 9:25 p.m., air tracker Flightradar24 data showed. Data from another flight-tracking platform, ADS-B Exchange, showed that the flight transmitted a squawk code 7700, a signal for a general emergency, around the time it was diverted. A Bulgarian MiG-29 fighter jet was scrambled to escort the aircraft. Following the evacuation of passengers after landing, a security search of the plane was launched, Austrian Airlines said in a statement quoted by Austrian news agency APA. https://vietnam.vnanet.vn/english/tin-va.text: In the News National Assembly President meets Polish Prime Minister 27/10/2026 National Assembly President Tran Thanh Man met with visiting Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk at the National Assembly House in Hanoi on the afternoon of October 26. National Assembly President Tran Thanh Man (R) meets with visiting Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in Hanoi on October 26. Photo: VNA Welcoming the Polish PM, who is on an official visit to Vietnam on October 24-26, NA President Man expressed satisfaction with the outcomes of the guest’s meeting with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and President To Lam and talks with Prime Minister Le Minh Hung. He affirmed that Vietnam’s National Assembly supports stronger inter-parliamentary cooperation with Poland’s parliament, with the legislative bodies playing a role in establishing a favourable legal framework, overseeing the implementation of agreements and commitments, and advancing bilateral cooperation effectively. According to him, Vietnam is accelerating efforts to improve its legal system, ensure effective administrative restructuring, renew its development model and enhance economic competitiveness, with the aim of achieving rapid and sustainable national development. Through its legislative and oversight functions, the National Assembly will help create a favourable and transparent investment and business environment, improve policy implementation and strengthen the confidence of domestic and foreign businesses, laying the foundation for long-term cooperation with Poland. The top legislator noted with pleasure that the Vietnam-Poland relationship is at its best to date, providing an important basis for the two countries to enter a new phase of development together. Building on their newly established Strategic Partnership, NA President Man proposed that the two sides focus on implementing the 2026–2030 Action Plan with concrete objectives. Maintaining effective high-level exchange mechanisms and implementing bilateral agreements will be essential to ensuring the sustainable, long-term development of bilateral ties. He called for stronger economic cooperation based on supply chain integration and investment, with a focus on attracting Polish investment in sectors where Poland has strengths and that align with Vietnam’s development needs. The target of raising bilateral trade to 6 billion USD should be pursued by establishing mechanisms to support businesses and creating a safe and transparent investment environment, he said, noting this would help Vietnam become an important link in regional and global supply chains, while serving as a strategic gateway for Polish companies seeking more convenient and effective access to ASEAN markets. The two countries should prioritise breakthrough sectors such as high technology, renewable energy, biotechnology and digital transformation. Greater cooperation in transport infrastructure, logistics and the marine economy will also provide an important foundation for stronger connectivity between the two countries and between Vietnam and the wider ASEAN region, he stated. The host thanked the Polish parliament for ratifying the EU-Vietnam Investment Protection Agreement (EVIPA) and called on Poland to work with the remaining EU member states to accelerate ratification so that the agreement can enter into force. He also encouraged Polish businesses to invest in Vietnam’s pharmaceutical industry, green energy, infrastructure and logistics. In science, technology and innovation, the NA President suggested greater support for Vietnamese businesses in capacity building, technology transfer and cooperation in pharmaceuticals, digital transformation and high-quality agriculture. He also called for closer collaboration in transport infrastructure, logistics and the marine economy. He expressed a desire to expand cultural and educational cooperation, welcomed Poland’s decision to increase scholarships for Vietnamese students, and called for visa facilitation to promote tourism and people-to-people exchanges. To ensure that parliamentary cooperation keeps pace with the development needs of both countries, NA President Man proposed more exchanges between the leadership of the two legislatures, specialised committees, friendship parliamentary groups, women parliamentarians and young lawmakers, as well as greater sharing of experience in building a rule-of-law state. He called on both sides to coordinate closely at the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and the Asia-Europe Parliamentary Partnership Meeting (ASEP), and asked PM Tusk to convey an invitation to leaders of the Polish parliament to visit Vietnam at a convenient time. For his part, PM Tusk reaffirmed Poland’s strong regard for its relationship with Vietnam, saying bilateral cooperation had considerable untapped potential. He stressed the need to translate the Strategic Partnership into joint projects, with clear priorities set out in the 2026–2030 Action Plan signed by the two sides during the visit. He called on Vietnam’s National Assembly to support the sharing of priorities across areas of cooperation so that both countries could focus their efforts effectively. PM Tusk noted that the Poland-Vietnam Parliamentary Friendship Group had made significant contributions to strengthening ties between the two legislatures. He particularly emphasised the importance of cooperation in education and training, scientific research and technology transfer among universities, research institutes and businesses in the two countries. He also shared his personal view that people-to-people exchanges, tourism and educational cooperation provided a solid foundation for the continued development of bilateral relations. Regarding specific areas of cooperation, PM Tusk expressed Poland’s interest in expanding collaboration with Vietnam in culture, education and training, security, defence and space cooperation. He also called for stronger links between businesses and vocational training institutions to develop a workforce that meets practical needs. He voiced support for closer cooperation between the two parliaments to facilitate exchanges of experience and support joint projects. He agreed on the importance of parliamentary cooperation in advancing high-level agreements, linking legislative experience-sharing with oversight of implementation and translating cooperation orientations into concrete results that deliver tangible benefits for people and businesses. The Polish PM spoke highly of the Vietnamese community in Poland, describing it as a community welcomed by Polish people, well integrated into society and serving as a bridge between the two countries. He pledged to work with the remaining EU member states to hasten ratification of EVIPA and to encourage the European Commission to consider lifting its yellow card warning regarding illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing against Vietnamese seafood./.
